<header>Canto 7] Accompanied by the two commentaries Rasikapriya and Rasamanjari 103</header>

May the account of Hari <note>Krishna</note> composed by the glorious Jayadeva,
Cause the impurities of the Kali Age to be diminished. || Some woman... || 8 ||

This moon, which mimics the luster of Murari's <note>Krishna's</note> lotus-face, pale from separation,
Though it hides my pain, as a friend of the heart's desire <note>Manobhava; another name for Kama, the god of love</note>,
It greatly increases the agony of love in my heart. || 5 ||

The battle of love; there she is steadfast. || 7 || Regarding the verse starting with "Sri": This account composed by the glorious Jayadeva, concerning the erotic play <note>of Krishna and Radha</note>, should diminish the impurities of the Kali Age, meaning it should bring peace. || 8 || In the *Sangitaraja*, it is said: "Where there is the Sri-raga and the rhythm is Druta-munthaka; where there is the description of Vasudeva, and the acts are related to the battle of love; where there are parts of the *pata* <note>syllables mimicking drum sounds</note> and musical notes, that is known as an excellent composition." This is the fourteenth composition named Harimitachampaka-shekhara. Now, Radha, suffering from separation, addresses the moon—starting with "In separation." Oh, soft-spoken one! Oh friend, this moon expands the extreme agony of love in my heart, for it is a close friend of the heart's desire <note>Kama</note>. She speaks reflecting on her state of separation from Murari. What is it like? It has a luster like that of the lotus-face of Murari, which is pale from separation. Therefore, even though it hides the pain, it implies that the luster of the face of Murari, which was pale due to my previous separation, destroys my pain; yet, because it is a friend of desire, it causes pain. It is said, "Since he is now attached to another, I cannot remain." || 7 || Regarding "Glorious Jayadeva": May the loveplay of Hari <note>Krishna</note>, recounted by the glorious Jayadeva, cause the impurities—the sins—of the Kali Age to be diminished for the listeners and readers, meaning it should destroy them. || 8 || Now, she says that even this moon causes more suffering—starting with "In separation." "Oh" is an expression of sorrow. This moon that I see expands—it extends—the agony of love in my heart to such a degree. What is it like? It possesses the luster of the lotus-face of Murari <note>Krishna</note>, which is pale due to separation from me. The idea is that seeing the moon, which resembles the lotus-face of Krishna, causes extreme distress through the memory of Krishna's lotus-face. What is it doing? It is hiding the pain. The idea is that the sight of the moon causes such a loss of discernment that the mind remembers only that Krishna who has committed an offense. She states the reason for it being a deceiver: "Heart-born" <note>Kama, the god of love</note>. The heart-born is a friend of desire. Since I did not follow Krishna even when he was nearby, by disobeying Kama's command, Kama has become my enemy. The moon, wishing to assist him, also creates suffering. The moon is famous as being born from the mind, and Kama is known as the "Mind-born." Because they are brothers, they share a friendship. Thus, the term "heart-born" is used for Kama. As the scripture says, "The moon was born from the mind, the sun from the eye." The word *vedana* means both knowledge and suffering. || 5 ||
